title: How Poland’s Restrictive Tax Treatment of Losses Penalizes Risk-Taking and Business Expansion
summary: Poland has one of the most restrictive approaches to the tax treatment of losses in the OECD. Loss carryover provisions allow businesses to deduct their losses in one year against taxable income in another, smoothing their taxable income over time. Their absence or restriction leads to firms with more variable profits and losses over time being taxed at higher rates, penalizing risky investment, such as research and development (R&D), and business expansion.
ai_summary: This article discusses Poland's restrictive tax treatment of losses, which penalizes risk-taking and business expansion due to limited loss carryover provisions. While not directly a transfer pricing issue, such tax policies can affect the overall profitability and risk profile of entities, influencing TP analyses.

ai_summary: The ITAT Mumbai ruled that Section 12AB registration for trusts and institutions cannot be made subject to a conditional rider. This decision follows a binding Bombay High Court judgment, removing caveats related to potential Supreme Court challenges.
